conviction_note: Two Indian travel peers that reported after MakeMyTrip last spoke (ixigo 2026-10-17, IHCL 2026-10-21) point to stronger hotel/bus demand than the consensus split assumes, while DGCA shows domestic air passengers down 4.8%/6.3% in Jul/Aug and MMYT habitually misses the headline revenue consensus. A crowded short (12.3 days to cover) and a -7.7% 5-day slide with no news set up a squeeze, but the option skew (+6.6 vol pts, put/call OI 9.3) pays for downside. Findings sum +0.8; the scaled number is (2*0.52-1)*9 = +0.36, a near-coin-flip with a slight long lean. The two measurements agree in sign; the scaled one is smaller because the air and revenue-headline negatives are real and the skew argues the other way.
bar: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) consensus revenue $267.4m and EPS $0.04 (Investing.com preview 2026-10-23, https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/makemytrip-earnings-on-deck-as-india-travel-faces-fuel-headwinds-93CH-4928927); revenue $269.09m and EPS $0.04 per Futu preview (https://news.futunn.com/en/post/1001729264/earnings-preview-makemytrip-to-report-financial-results-pre-market-on, snippet only). The two sources roughly agree. Investing also reports analyst segment estimates of hotels about +20% and bus about +26% in constant currency, with air declining, plus a rupee down about 9% YoY (reported revenue about +17%, about +25% cc). Year-ago Q2 FY26 revenue was $229.3m (https://www.phocuswire.com/makemytrip-fiscal-2026-second-quarter-earnings). The company gave no guidance (Q1 call: 'one quarter could be better or worse', https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392). BofA (Salgaonkar) previewed a 'soft 2Q' on airline supply and fuel on 2026-09-28 and cut its target from $71 to $60 (https://tipranks.com/news/the-fly/makemytrip-price-target-lowered-to-60-from-71-at-bofa-thefly-news?amp=). The EPS consensus is IFRS diluted EPS depressed by convertible-note finance costs and FX; the bar the stock trades on is more likely gross bookings and adjusted EBIT, for which no consensus was found.
positioning_check: Short interest 9.0M shares, 12.3 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 FINRA settlement, up from 8.5M on 07-31 and 7.6M on 06-15 (CurvedTrading summary of FINRA data in search snippet, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mmyt/short-interest/; the page itself returned 403). An earlier Equibles snapshot (07-02) put it at 8.5% of float (https://equibles.com/stocks/mmyt/shortinterest). No September or October settlement was found. Baseline: 25d skew +6.56 vol pts (downside paid), put/call OI 9.27 on only 1,161 contracts, event-implied move 11.78% with the ATM spread at 60% of mid (indicative only). Spot $43.01: -52.2% from the 52-week high, -8.0% over 20 days, -7.7% over 5 days, with no named catalyst. AAII on 2026-10-23 found no news or rating change behind the -5% day (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/549033-why-makemytrip-limited8217s-mmyt-stock-is-down-503). Sell-side consensus is 'Moderate Buy', average target $73.50 (MarketBeat 2026-10-19). Read: a crowded and rising short plus heavy put demand into a print with a low, already-cut bar.

findings.finding: Indian Hotels (IHCL) reported Q2 FY27 (same Jul-Sep quarter) on 2026-10-21: domestic same-store RevPAR +25% YoY, accelerating from about +14% in Q1 FY27, and raised its FY27 revenue growth guide from 12-14% to 15-17%. This is an industry read for MMYT's Hotels & Packages, its largest segment (adjusted margin $134.5m of $309.7m in Q1, +21.3% cc). The consensus split has MMYT hotels at about +20% cc, roughly flat on Q1's rate, while the hotel industry's pricing accelerated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-03): Hotels & Packages adjusted margin +21.3% cc carried the quarter and the stock closed +8.5% despite a headline revenue miss, partly a sector rally on Iran-deal news. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-19): revenue missed and the stock fell 7.7%. Segment surprises have not been isolated in the record.
findings.why_not_priced: MMYT fell about 4% on 10-21 and about 3.5% on 10-22 after IHCL printed, and fell 5% on 10-23 with no news. Had US holders of this ADR read the IHCL acceleration across to MMYT's hotel line, the stock would have firmed into the print rather than sliding 7.7% in five days. The Investing preview of 10-23 still frames the quarter on fuel and airline headwinds and quotes a +20% hotel estimate.
findings.independence: Proxy: IHCL is a premium hotel owner/operator, not an MMYT counterparty, and MMYT's mix is mid-market and alternative stays. RevPAR +25% figure from https://www.investywise.com/?p=121617 and https://taxguru.in/?p=1092913 (search snippets); Q1 +14% from https://insights.dsij.in/markets/reports/report-details/the-indian-hotels-company-ltd/44652. ixigo's hotel GTV 2.6x (finding 2) points the same way but comes from a small base.

findings.finding: ixigo (Le Travenues), a listed Indian OTA, reported Q2 FY27 on 2026-10-17: GTV +22% YoY to Rs 5,304 cr, flights GTV +37%, bus GTV +32%, hotels GTV 2.6x; it said bus demand rose partly because of higher airfares and scarce confirmed train tickets. The direct-peer read: OTA air booking value held up through fares despite falling passenger counts, and bus is tracking above the consensus +26% cc for MMYT's redBus (+32.4% cc in Q1).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MMYT Q1 FY27: air adjusted margin +10.8% cc on slightly lower volume (higher fares), bus +32.4% cc; the stock rose 8.5%. ixigo itself rallied about 13-15% on 2026-10-19 on these numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer that printed after MMYT last spoke (2026-08-03). MMYT fell from $46.60 (10-16 close) to $43.01 over the week ixigo rallied double digits on its own print, so the read-across did not reach the ADR.
findings.independence: Separate document from IHCL. ixigo is a share-gainer from a small base, so its flights +37% overstates the industry and partly conflicts with the DGCA passenger series in finding 3, which is the broader series. That is why this finding is sized below finding 3's absolute value on air and rests mostly on bus. Company release: https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/IXIGO_17102026131559_Regulation_30_Media_Release_17102026.pdf (returned 503); exceptional gain context in https://yourstory.com/2026/10/ixigo-q2-profit-at-rs-63-cr-on-robust-show-in-hotel-booking-biz.

findings.finding: DGCA/ICRA: domestic air passengers fell 4.8% YoY in July 2026 (120.0 lakh) and 6.3% in August (121.3 lakh), against roughly +1.6% in Apr-Jun (derived from ICRA's 5M FY27 total of 667.9 lakh, -1.1%). The August load factor was 79.0% vs 84.1%, ATF was +33.4% YoY in September, and international traffic on Indian carriers was -20.9% for Apr-Aug (improving from -31.6% in Apr-May). So Q2 air volumes deteriorated about 7 points vs Q1 on MMYT's second-largest segment (Q1 air adjusted margin $98.5m, about 32% of the total; 30% domestic air share).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-05-19): West Asia-hit air and outbound with a revenue miss, stock -7.7%. Q1 FY27: air volume slightly down, but fare-driven margin +10.8% cc and the stock rose.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: BofA's 09-28 preview and the 10-23 Investing preview both name airline capacity cuts and fuel, and consensus expects air to decline. What may not be fully in is the size of the Q1-to-Q2 swing (about +1.6% to about -5.6%) against a revenue bar that assumes cc growth accelerates to about +25%.
findings.independence: Broad public series. Corroborated by https://www.angelone.in/news/economy/india-s-domestic-air-traffic-drops-6-34-to-12-126-million-passengers-in-august-2026 and https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/indian-domestic-aviation-sees-july-slump-amid-capacity-lean-period-as-air-traffic-falls-by-48-per-cent-indigo-extends-market-dominance-to-over-67-pc. Partly offset by higher fares (finding 2).

findings.finding: MMYT has missed the headline revenue consensus on each of the last three prints: Q3 FY26 $295.7m vs about $310m, Q4 FY26 $250.1m vs $281.0m, and Q1 FY27 $285.6m (reported as a miss). The Q2 bar of $267.4m implies +16.6% reported and about +25% cc, against +16.1% cc in Q1. Applying last year's Q1-to-Q2 seasonal ratio (229.3/268.8) to Q1 FY27's $285.6m gives about $244m, about 9% under the bar. A fourth headline revenue miss is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 revenue miss: -6% premarket and -7.7% close-to-close (2026-05-19). Q1 FY27 revenue miss with an EPS beat: +8.5% (2026-08-03). Q3 FY26 revenue miss: later 12% fall on target cuts (Stocktwits). The holders have both sold and looked through the habitual miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus revenue line has not been reset despite three misses: Investing notes revenue estimates rose 0.33% over 60 days. If the market had priced a structural miss, the bar would sit nearer $245-255m. Partly mitigated because the stock rose on the last miss.
findings.independence: Q3 figures from https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/why-did-makemytrip-stock-fall-today/cmUxPsFR4Qb and https://fxempire.com/stocks/mmyt/earnings; seasonal base from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001495153/000119312526329581/mmyt-ex99_1.htm and https://www.phocuswire.com/makemytrip-fiscal-2026-second-quarter-earnings. This is my own arithmetic, not a company number.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is one-sided: short interest 9.0M shares and 12.3 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement, rising for three consecutive settlements; put/call open interest 9.3; spot -52% from the 52-week high and -7.7% in the five sessions to 10-23 with no news; EPS bar cut to $0.04 and BofA already previewed a soft quarter. An adequate print, or management saying outbound is recovering, has a squeeze mechanism inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-03) came after a weak spring with heavy shorts and rose 8.5%, about 3% premarket ('surges 3% on strong earnings beat') rising into the close.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew (+6.6, downside paid) is the market saying the opposite, so this is a contrarian read. It is filed small because the latest short-interest settlement found is two months old and the drawdown has no identified cause, which by itself is worth nothing.
findings.independence: Option figures from the sealed baseline; 10-23 no-news drop from https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/549033-why-makemytrip-limited8217s-mmyt-stock-is-down-503.

findings.finding: Reported (IFRS) profit will again be depressed below operating income by non-cash interest on the roughly $1.4bn out-of-the-money convertible notes and by rupee depreciation (about 9% YoY; Q1 reported net income fell 65% to $9.1m). The EPS consensus of $0.04 already embeds this, so it is a one-off with no path to guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 reported net income -65% while the stock rose 8.5%; the holders look at adjusted EBIT.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced via the $0.04 EPS bar. A sharper rupee move in Q2 than Q1 could add FX losses beyond it.
findings.independence: Convertible structure from the Q1 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392).

findings.finding: On the Q1 FY27 call management said it would be 'happy to remain' at about 1.8% adjusted EBIT/gross bookings 'or gradually increase', and that it prioritises market share, customer acquisition and AI investment over near-term operating leverage. Marketing was 5.4% of GB vs 5.2%. A soft air quarter therefore has little margin cushion to protect adjusted EBIT.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin-moderation commentary after Q3 FY26 drew target cuts from Morgan Stanley and Citi and a 12% fall (Stocktwits, 2026-03-05).
findings.why_not_priced: Stated publicly, so mostly priced. Filed because it caps the upside in findings 1-2 on the profit line.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 6 (Q1 call transcript); different statement.

outside_window.finding: MakeMyTrip (India) confidential DRHP filed 2026-07-17 for a reported $1bn+ India IPO, mostly offer-for-sale, with proceeds possibly funding repurchases of the convertibles. No public DRHP, price band or SEBI observation has been found, so a valuation mark or fungibility news is unlikely inside the window unless management gives a timeline on the call.

baseline_tension: The evidence (peer prints, crowded short) leans mildly against the downside skew and the -8% run-up. The skew and the habitual revenue miss argue the other way, so p_up is held at 52 rather than the high 50s the peer data alone would suggest.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy vs broad series): IHCL premium-hotel proxy trimmed from +1.2 to +1.0. ixigo trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6 because its flights +37% partly conflicts with the broader DGCA passenger series, which stays filed.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): DGCA air finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6 and the revenue-miss habit from -0.7 to -0.5, given 12.3 days to cover.
Rule 7 (sign against skew): net-positive lean kept small, with p_up at 52, because the +6.6 skew and the 9.3 put/call OI say downside.
Untrustworthy FPI history: base rate rebuilt from confirmed prints (05-19 -7.7%, 08-03 +8.5%) and the option-implied 11.8%, giving abs_move 9.
Rule 6 (bar): two roughly agreeing revenue/EPS sources found, so no cap applied; the India IPO is kept in outside_window.
